_comment_columnMap: What a person confirmed from the profiler's proposal. Held as configuration rather than code because the next client's export will not spell its columns this way. The profiler proposed all eight of these from the dump itself; nothing here was typed from knowledge of the client.
_comment_priorities: This client's priority scheme has five levels and the platform has four, so the bottom two collapse. 94% of the dump sits at '5 - Planning', which is a fact about how they file rather than about how urgent their estate is — a reader of any figure cut by priority needs to know that.
_comment_subCategoryClasses: The declaration a person owns, in two separable halves. classId says which class the ledger prices this demand as; nodeIds says which component in the estate it lands on. Either may be stated without the other, and the difference matters: the component decides the tower and therefore the policy, the service level and the knowledge pack, while the class decides what it is and what it costs. A sub-category with a component and no class is placed correctly and classified no further than its theme — which is the honest outcome when we know what a ticket is about and not what it is.
_comment_withdrawn: Three declarations were withdrawn after reading what the tickets actually say rather than what the sub-category is called. Each keeps its component and carries _was and _because so the reversal is on the record rather than a silent deletion.
_comment_componentOnly: The demand ledger's 24 costed classes were derived from an extract that analysed application and data management alone — 2,721 of the 28,028 incidents. It prices none of the digital-workplace volume, which is why those entries carry a component and no class. Naming a class for them would mean inventing one, and the extract cannot support the effort figure a costed class needs: it supplies no resolution or close timestamp, so handling time is not derivable at all.
_comment_classed: Where a costed class genuinely corresponds. The first three recover a link already in the data: the estate's known errors record 2,484, 926 and 658 occurrences, exactly the volumes of Account Lock-Out, M365-OneDrive and IEM in this dump. The rest were checked against what the tickets actually say, not against the sub-category's name.

subCategoryClasses._because: dc_triple_av is costed at 41 incidents a year and names agents contending for CPU. These 1,567 are failed Cisco Secure Endpoint Tetra definition updates, which is a different failure entirely — and the class would have offered them the agent de-duplication runbook.
These 674 read "Office apps login blocked by Cisco AMP" and "Cannot login to any MS office app" — access blocked by the agent, not CPU contention.

dc_sw_provision is catalogue software provisioning. These 264 read "Unable to turn on PC / Blue screen", "WiFi driver not functioning" and "Dell PC sound not working" — device faults, not provisioning.
